html:
SMTO-SKL-0139 — That file is too big for SMTO to send through Slack

GUID: acdd113e-89b8-5dea-9e3d-92874c2cc4c9
Slug: slack-file-too-large
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • SMTO can move files to and from Slack only up to 25 MB. This file is bigger, or Slack sent more data than the file's listed size, so SMTO stopped. Nothing was uploaded or saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. For an upload, make the file 25 MB or smaller (for example, compress or split it), then ask the Agent to upload it again. SMTO checks the size before sending anything to Slack.
  2. For a larger file you want from Slack, open it in Slack and download it there. SMTO's 25 MB limit applies to every Slack file transfer.
  3. If the file is under 25 MB and this still appears, ask the Agent to look up the file's details again, then download it once more. Slack's listed size may have been out of date, and a fresh lookup gets the current one.

What success looks like

  • The file uploads to Slack or appears in the conversation.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file's name and size, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Slack file exceeds the 25 MiB transfer limit, or a download streamed more bytes than the size declared by files.info.

What this means

  • File size exceeds 25 MiB, or a download streams more bytes than its declared size even below the maximum. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • File size exceeds 25 MiB, or a download streams more bytes than its declared size even below the maximum.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare source/streamed bytes with both the 25 MiB bound and declared size.

How to fix it

  • Keep transfers within MAX_BYTES (25 MiB) in skills/slack/files.py. For a size mismatch on a file under the limit, re-read files.info (slack.file_info) and retry slack.download_file; a persistent mismatch indicates inconsistent Slack-side file metadata.
  • Use a file within 25 MiB and refresh inconsistent metadata before downloading again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The complete intended file fits the bound and matches its exact size.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
